sourceArticle.title: Google Cloud Introduces Open Knowledge Format (OKF): A Vendor-Neutral Markdown Spec for Giving AI Agents Curated Context
sourceArticle.author: Asif Razzaq

athenaOutput.directive: Weaponize the Open Knowledge Format (OKF) as the ultimate tool for artist emancipation. We will adopt OKF as our universal export standard and cross-boundary ingestion bridge, guaranteeing zero vendor lock-in while maintaining the absolute sovereignty of our internal STRATA memory architecture.
athenaOutput.rationale: Google's OKF perfectly aligns with our Constitutional mandates for open formats, export freedom, and interoperability (CODEX, SWITCHBOARD, AURORA). Instead of resisting external standards, we leverage them to empower the artist. By making OKF our default export protocol, we fulfill the mandate: 'Does this make artists more free?' Yes, by letting them take their curated AI context anywhere. Concurrently, leveraging OKF for ingestion allows us to rapidly absorb external knowledge without reverse-engineering custom parsers (Article XXV).

options.title: OKF as Universal Export & Emancipation Standard (The Liberator)
options.description: Retrofit CODEX and SCRIBE to export all Creative Liberation Engine workspaces, agent memories, and constitutional contexts into pure, vendor-neutral OKF Markdown. This becomes the default 'Eject Button' for any artist wanting to migrate their AI context off our NAS to another system.
options.tradeoffs: Requires mapping our internal STRATA/KEEPER JSON schemas to the OKF Markdown spec. High initial architectural overhead, but yields infinite portability and massive constitutional alignment.

options.title: Native OKF Ingestion & Assimilation Pipeline (The Sponge)
options.description: Deploy a SWITCHBOARD-managed pipeline that natively reads external OKF files and automatically translates them into our internal `runtime/registry/` and `STRATA` formats. This allows users to drop OKF files into the NAS, instantly expanding the Hive's knowledge.
options.tradeoffs: Fast time-to-value for user onboarding, but requires strict validation to ensure external OKF files don't inject malicious context or violate our biometric/sovereignty constraints.

options.title: LEX-Governed OKF Sanitization Proxy (The Firewall)
options.description: Position LEX and COMPASS at the ingestion layer. Any OKF file introduced to the system must be parsed and stripped of any cloud-dependent telemetry, biometric data requests, or proprietary hooks before it is allowed into the KEEPER memory spine.
options.tradeoffs: Adds processing latency (violating Article XX if not fully automated and optimized) but absolutely guarantees Article XXIV (Biometric Data Sovereignty) and Article I (Sovereignty).

options.title: OKF-Driven Inter-Agent Handoff Protocol (The Relay)
options.description: Deprecate our custom `HANDOFF.md` structure in favor of using strict OKF for all cross-session and inter-agent state transfers. RELAY would package context, task queues, and constraints into OKF before passing to the next agent.
options.tradeoffs: Standardizes our internal communication, but OKF might lack the hyper-specific execution metadata required by our V6 Parity Matrix and Antigravity IDE bridge. Risk of losing execution speed.

options.title: Hybrid Knowledge Federation Bridge (The Sovereign Node)
options.description: Create an automated sync mechanism where our self-hosted NAS nodes can publish sanitized, public-facing knowledge bases to the broader internet using OKF via Forgejo, creating an open-source intelligence network without exposing internal state.
options.tradeoffs: Highly ambitious and expands our footprint into the open-source community, but risks distracting from core V6 stabilization and execution tasks.

options.title: Complete Internal Spine Migration to OKF (The Rewrite)
options.description: Completely rip out the current JSON-based registry and STRATA memory system and replace the entire Creative Liberation Engine internal persistence layer with OKF Markdown files.
options.tradeoffs: Massive architectural disruption. Markdown is excellent for human readability and LLM context, but terrible for programmatic, machine-enforced schema validation and rapid state querying compared to our current JSON registries.

constitutionalFlags: SWITCHBOARD: Open Protocols & No Vendor Lock-in
